questions.question: A poem repeats the end sounds light and night. What sound device is present?
choices: End rhyme
Alliteration
Assonance
Onomatopoeia

questions.question: Which description best defines meter in poetry?
choices: The number of characters in a poem
A recurring pattern of stressed and unstressed syllables
The poem's line-ending punctuation
A comparison using like or as

questions.question: A line scans as da-DUM da-DUM da-DUM da-DUM da-DUM. Which meter does it most closely represent?
choices: Trochaic tetrameter
Free verse
Iambic pentameter
Anapestic trimeter

questions.question: Why might a poet use internal rhyme?
choices: To remove all rhythm from a poem
To make every line have the same number of words
To identify the speaker's point of view
To create sound links within a line

questions.question: Which pair is a slant rhyme?
choices: Shape / keep
Moon / June
Light / night
Stone / alone

questions.question: A poem's regular beat suddenly breaks at a moment of panic. What can that change do?
choices: Prove the poem has no sound pattern
Make the disruption in feeling or action more noticeable
Show that the speaker is not present
Turn the poem into a sonnet

questions.question: Which feature is most useful for identifying a rhyme scheme?
choices: The number of stanzas only
The first word of each line
The sounds at the ends of lines
The poem's title

questions.question: A poet repeats long vowel sounds in 'slow road home.' Which device is most evident?
choices: Consonance
End rhyme
Refrain
Assonance

questions.question: Which line contains alliteration?
choices: Silver stars shimmer softly
The river bends toward the sea
A bird flew over the hill
The night was cold and clear

questions.question: A refrain is best described as
choices: a pause within a metrical foot
a line or phrase repeated at intervals
a comparison between unlike things
the final couplet of every poem

questions.question: Why should a reader consider both rhythm and meaning when interpreting a poem?
choices: Rhythm always tells the literal plot
Meaning is determined only by rhyme
Sound patterns can reinforce, complicate, or contrast with the ideas
Sound devices replace evidence from the words

questions.question: A line has 12 syllables, but its stresses do not form a steady pattern. What is the safest conclusion?
choices: It must be iambic pentameter
It cannot be poetry
It has exactly six rhyming couplets
Syllable count alone does not establish a regular meter

questions.question: Which revision would most clearly create a couplet?
choices: Add a second consecutive line that rhymes with the first
Split one line into two unrhymed lines
Repeat the title after every stanza
Remove the final word from the first line

questions.question: What is a caesura?
choices: A repeated stanza at the end
A pause within a line of poetry
A word that imitates a sound
A pair of lines with matching syllables

questions.question: A poet uses a steady beat in a marching scene. Which effect is most likely intended?
choices: To make the speaker unreliable by definition
To create an unrelated rhyme scheme
To echo the scene's regular movement
To prove the poem is written in free verse

questions.question: Which method best supports a claim about a poem's meter?
choices: Count only the lines in the poem
Look up the poet's birthplace
Read only the final stanza
Mark syllables and stresses across several lines

questions.question: Which statement distinguishes free verse from blank verse?
choices: Free verse lacks a fixed meter; blank verse typically uses unrhymed iambic pentameter
Free verse always rhymes; blank verse never has rhythm
Free verse is prose; blank verse is drama only
They are two names for a sonnet

questions.question: The repeated consonant sounds in 'blank and think' are an example of
choices: assonance
consonance
refrain
meter

questions.question: A poem's final word choices create a repeated ABAB pattern. What does that pattern describe?
choices: Point of view
Caesura
Rhyme scheme
Enjambment

questions.question: A poet shifts from smooth, regular lines to clipped, uneven lines as a speaker becomes angry. Which interpretation is strongest?
choices: The poem has stopped using language devices
The poet has changed the poem's subject automatically
The uneven lines cannot be analyzed
The changing rhythm may mirror the speaker's emotional shift
